primitives.name: Pose Tracking Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: US 12,299,852 B2 BODY POSE TRACKING OF PLAYERS FROM SPORTS BROADCAST VIDEO FEED CROSS-REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATIONS This application claims priority to U.S.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{P}^{(t)}': 'Vector of tracked body joint coordinates (dimensionless)', '\\mathbf{V}^{(t)}': 'Raw pose estimates from video frame t (dimensionless)', '\\mathbf{L}': 'Location data (player positions in play area)', '\\mathcal{T}': 'Tracking operator'}
primitives.assumptions: (1) Video frames are temporally aligned, (2) Player identities are consistent across frames, (3) Location data has lower noise than raw pose estimates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when camera calibration errors exceed spatial resolution of the playing surface.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Kalman filtering framework for latent variable estimation, where pose tracking corresponds to posterior mean under Gaussian assumptions.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error reduction in predicted player trajectories compared to raw pose inputs.

primitives.name: Denoising Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method may comprise receiving, by a computing system, raw body pose data of a plurality of players in a video frame of a sporting event video feed.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{\\mathbf{P}}^{(t)}': 'Refined pose estimate (dimensionless)', '\\mathbf{V}^{(t)}': 'Raw pose vector (dimensionless)', '\\mathcal{R}(\\mathbf{L})': 'Regularization term based on player locations (dimensionless)', '\\lambda': 'Denoising regularization parameter (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: (1) The regularization enforces smoothness across player locations, (2) The hyperparameter \lambda balances data fidelity vs. prior knowledge.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when \lambda approaches zero, reverting to noisy raw estimates; also fails if the mapping \mathcal{R} is misspecified.

layer2.mapping: Relates to GSE's state-transition kernel for predicting next-frame states, where denoising acts as a measurement update step.
layer2.telemetry: Improvement in signal-to-noise ratio of tracked joints relative to input video.

primitives.name: Correspondence Matching Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method may also comprise determining, by the computing system, correspondence between at least one location from the location data to a raw body pose data of at least one player of the plurality of players.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M(i,j)': 'Assignment probability between player i and j', '\\mathbf{x}_i^{(t)}': 'Raw pose coordinate vector for player i at time t', '\\mathbf{y}_j^{(t)}': 'Location coordinate vector for player j at time t', '\\sigma': 'Spatial standard deviation parameter (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: (1) Assignments maximize likelihood under Gaussian observation models, (2) Number of players is known and constant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when multiple players occupy identical locations, requiring additional discriminative features.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic data association for multi-target tracking, where assignment probabilities serve as posterior beliefs.
layer2.telemetry: Correct assignment rate measured against ground-truth player identities.

primitives.name: Location Retrieval Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method may further comprise retrieving, by the computing system, location data for the plurality of players in the video frame.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{L}^{(t)}': 'Retrieved player location vectors (meters)', '\\mathbf{I}^{(t)}': 'Input video frame (RGB tensor)', '\\mathcal{R}': 'Retrieval function mapping image to locations'}
primitives.assumptions: (1) The retrieval function is deterministic given the frame, (2) Locations are unique within a single time slice.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when occlusions cause missing player positions or when the retrieval network encounters distribution shift.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's perceptual state representation, where location retrieval provides the current belief state over player positions.
layer2.telemetry: Precision-recall curve for recovered player locations against manual annotations.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is fusing low-variance but sparse location data with high-variance but dense pose estimates. This is formulated as a constrained optimization problem using a quadratic loss. The solution leverages the correspondence matrix to enforce identity consistency across frames. Failure occurs when the spatial resolution of the playing field cannot distinguish between players, leading to ambiguous assignments. To mitigate this, higher-order temporal coherence constraints are often added, smoothing trajectories over windows of frames.
